biodivMapR

An R package for α- and β-diversity mapping using remotely-sensed images

1 Main principles of biodivMapR

biodivMapR aims at being sensor agnostic

biodivMapR is an R package aiming at processing remote sensing data provided as raster files in order to produce spectral diversity metrics.

The first versions of the method were initially dedicated to optical data processing and the spectral dimension was the key dimension to produce features to relate to ecological information. However, since biodivMapR v2.0, the workflow aims at being sensor agnostic: users can provide raster data obtained from optical sensors (multispectral, hyperspectral sensors), LiDAR or radar data.

Therefore, diversity metrics are no longer spectral. Remotely sensed diversity metrics from a collection of rasters sharing the same projection, spatial resolution and extent but different sensors can also be provided.

biodivMapR can work with discrete and continuous representations of data

biodivMapR was initially developed to produce α\alpha and β\beta diversity maps, based on the implementation of the method developed by Féret & Asner (2014).

Since the earliest versions of the package, our aim is to provide a tool useful for the ecologist community, with the capacity to evolve and provide alternative ways to handle remote sensing data.

Therefore, two main representations of data are handled by biodivMapR:

  • a discrete representation based on clustering techniques, aiming at producing ‘spectral species’: pixels are grouped into clusters, assuming that user-defined features allow unsupervised clustering to identify ecologically relevant groups corresponding to species, species communities, structurally or functionally similar entities. This representation allows to directly compute diversity metrics usually derived from species inventories (Shannon index, Bray-Curtis dissimilarity…).

  • a continuous representation using directly the feature/trait space, aiming at producing Functional diversity metrics Richness, Evenness, and Divergence as defined in Villeger et al. (2008), as well as Dispersion and Rao entropy. These functional diversity metrics are computed with the package fundiversity.

biodivMapR aims at providing an open source tool where additional diversity metrics either based on the discrete or continuous representation of data can be easily implemented. If you need specific metrics, want to suggest additional ones, or contribute to their implementation, please feel free to contact the authors of the package

biodivMapR can produce large scale diversity maps from cloud infrastructures

Efforts have been made in the recent versions to allow the integration of biodivMapR into cloud infrastructures, in order to produce large scale maps.

Please contact the authors to exchange and collaborate on the integration into cloud infrastructures and the production of large scale maps.

biodivMapR needs (your) validation

As a software developed from researchers and mainly dedicated to researchers, biodivMapR requires validation to identify its potential and limitations.

biodivMapR uses unsupervised methods. It is not based on modern learning techniques. The validation is an on-going process, and contributions are welcome to help us to provide recommendations for the application of biodivMapR in different contexts.

2 Install

The package remotes first needs to be installed from the CRAN

install.packages("remotes")

biodivMapR should then be ready for installation with the following command line in your R session:

remotes::install_github('jbferet/biodivMapR')

3 Tutorial

A tutorial vignette is available here.

4 Citation

If you use biodivMapR, please cite the following references:

Féret, J.-B., de Boissieu, F., 2019. biodivMapR: an R package for α‐ and β‐diversity mapping using remotely‐sensed images. Methods Ecol. Evol. 00:1-7. https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.13310

Féret, J.-B., Asner, G.P., 2014. Mapping tropical forest canopy diversity using high-fidelity imaging spectroscopy. Ecol. Appl. 24, 1289–1296. https://doi.org/10.1890/13-1824.1
